messages.subject: Contingency table question
parts:
Hi,

Deducer is great, really enjoying the feature set, especially the robust plot builder.  The price is pretty nice, too. ;)  I've been using various stat packages for years and it is nice to finally see something like this.  I've always wanted to get into R and this is motivating me to actually try.  Anyway...

I had a question about the contingency table analysis.  Is there any way to define a column as a frequency column to summarize the frequency of a particular set of conditions instead of having each data point have an individual row? 
For instance, if I have a data set in which I have 5 of organism 1 with status 1 and 15 of organism 1 with status 2, and  8  of organism 2 with status 1 and 23 with status 2 could I basically summarize that with 4 rows and 3 columns (the final being the frequency) or do I need a row for each data point?

messages.author: 1a09129d38549286
messages.subject: Re: Contingency table question
parts:
Hi,

You can do that with the function xtabs. It's not included among Deducer dialogs, but it's fairly easy to use. If your data frame DF has the variables "organism", "status", and "freq", just type:

xtabs(freq~organism+status, data=DF)

Helios

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Contingency table question
parts:
for the chi-squared, you can select "conservative" and monte-carlo,
and that will give you the level alpha p-value. You can't do that for
the fisher's exact test, but you can change it in the command line
with the conservative=TRUE option:

tables<-add.fishers.exact(tables,conservative=TRUE)



ian
